pages.title: Pieces
pages.content:
Pieces

Ready jewelry produced in small runs at our bench at 22 Wexley Street. Each piece is shaped in recycled gold or silver and made for daily wear.

Ready Work for Daily Wear

Our collection of ready pieces is designed for everyday life, filed and finished by hand at 22 Wexley Street. The selection includes the Tuesday Band 2 mm in 18k recycled yellow gold for $640, the Linen Signet in 9k gold with an oval face for $720, and the Lamp Studs in 18k gold at $380 a pair. We also craft the Bench Chain in 9k gold measuring 45 cm for $560, the Pebble Pendant in 18k gold on a 42 cm chain for $690, and the Shank Ring in silver with an 18k gold cap for $290. You can browse our work by type across rings, chains, studs, and pendants. Each design is produced in modest quantities so that every surface receives proper attention under the bench lamp.

How does sizing work for ready pieces?

We provide complimentary sizing on all ready pieces within 30 days of purchase. When you order a ring, you want it to sit comfortably against your skin whether you are at your desk, on a bicycle, or working with your hands. If the fit is not entirely right when it arrives, you can bring or send it back to our workshop in Port Ellery. Sofia Duarte or Hana Okada will assess the fit and adjust the shank up or down so that it settles naturally on your hand. There is no charge for adjustments completed within the initial thirty-day period.

pages.title: Commissions
pages.content:
Commissions

We work directly with you to draw and fabricate individual pieces in recycled gold and silver. Every commission begins at our bench with an unhurried conversation.

From Bench Talk to Drawing

The process begins with a bench talk at 22 Wexley Street. This initial consultation lasts 45 minutes and is completely free. We discuss your thoughts, look at materials, and consider how the piece will sit on your hand or neck. Following our meeting, Ravi Menon prepares detailed pencil drawings and an exact quote within 10 days. Once you approve the drawings, a 40 % deposit is taken to secure the materials and begin workshop production. Plain bands in recycled 18k gold begin from $980, hand-engraved signets from $1,450, and custom stone settings from $1,900 with stones quoted separately.

Wax Fitting, Fabrication, and Completion

After drawings are approved, we carve a green wax model for you to try on in person at the shop. This fitting allows you to assess the volume, balance, and proportions before we melt any metal. Once you confirm the wax, Ines Marlow and the bench team proceed to casting and fabrication. Making and finishing takes 6 to 8 weeks from the date of the approved drawing. Every claw, bevel, and shank is filed and burnished by hand, ensuring the completed piece is prepared for decades of continuous wear.

What past commissions have been drawn here?

Two bands from one bracelet

Our bespoke work responds directly to the stories brought into our workshop.

A signet for a left-handed baker

Lea Brandt engraved a flat-faced signet to be worn comfortably on the right hand.

The pendant that came back

Kwame Asante re-set the original heirloom stone into newly formed claws.

Our bespoke work responds directly to the stories brought into our workshop. Past commissions include two wedding bands melted down from a single heirloom bracelet, drawn by Ravi and cast by Ines. We also crafted a flat-faced signet ring for a left-handed baker, engraved by Lea Brandt to be worn comfortably on the right hand during long kneading shifts. Another project involved re-making a worn pendant around its original heirloom stone, which Kwame Asante securely re-set into newly formed claws. We welcome family gold and stones whenever sound fabrication allows.

Book a bench talk →

pages.title: Prices
pages.content:
Prices

Our workshop pricing is clear, direct, and based on bench time and honest materials. We quote all bespoke work in writing before any metal is touched.

Bands and Signets

Bespoke band commissions start at $980 using solid recycled 18k yellow, white, or rose gold. The price reflects hand-alloying, rolling, bending, soldering, and hand-filing the shank to your exact measurements. Hand-engraved signet rings begin at $1,450. Lea Brandt carves initials, monograms, or motifs directly into the solid gold face using traditional steel gravers, creating deep lines that endure through years of contact.

Stone Setting and Alterations

Custom stone-setting commissions start at $1,900, which covers the design, mounting fabrication, and Kwame Asante's setting work. Gemstones and diamonds are sourced individually and quoted separately during the drawing stage. For alterations on existing jewelry, we provide gold resizing up to two sizes for $85 within 7 days, claw re-tipping and re-polishing for $120 within 10 to 14 days, and inside band engraving up to 20 characters for $60. All work takes place on Wexley Street.

Book a bench talk →

pages.title: Repairs & Care
pages.content:
Repairs & Care

We repair, restore, and maintain gold and silver jewelry to keep it in daily circulation. Work is carried out directly on our benches at 22 Wexley Street.

Resizing, gold, up to two sizes

7 days

$85

Re-polish and re-tip claws

10–14 days

Claws checked under the loupe

With every re-tip

Included in the $120

Bench Services and Repair Pricing

We repair pieces we did not make, working exclusively in solid gold and silver. Common bench repairs include resizing gold rings up to two sizes for $85, completed within 7 days. For rings with worn prongs or dulled metal, we re-polish surfaces and re-tip claws for $120, requiring 10 to 14 days to ensure stones remain firmly secured. Sofia Duarte inspects each piece under magnification to check solder seams, hinge pins, and shank thickness before proceeding with any repair.

Caring for Your Jewelry Every Day

Jewelry is made to be lived in, but everyday dirt, lotion, and soap film will gather behind stones and along inner shanks over time. To clean your gold and silver pieces, soak them in a small bowl of warm water mixed with mild dishwashing liquid. Gently scrub behind the settings and around claws using a soft-bristled baby toothbrush. Rinse thoroughly with clean warm water and pat dry with a soft undyed cloth. Never use bleach, harsh chemical dips, or ultrasonic cleaners on delicate gems. Remove your rings when handling heavy abrasive tools or lifting weights to avoid warping the gold shank.

What materials do you accept for repair?

We work exclusively with recycled and solid gold or silver. We do not work on brass, copper, stainless steel, plated costume jewelry, or base metal fashion pieces. Solder used on plated items burns through thin surfaces, making lasting repairs impossible. If you bring a gold or silver piece to our shop, Sofia Duarte or Ines Marlow will examine the metal quality, verify the hallmarks or test the alloy, and give you an honest appraisal of whether the piece can be safely restored.

Bring a piece in →

pages.title: The Bench
pages.content:
The Bench

Tsuya Jewellers was founded in 2011 by Ines Marlow at 22 Wexley Street in Port Ellery. Today, six makers sit at our benches to design, fabricate, set, engrave, and finish every piece.

Six people, one bench

Ines Marlow

Founder, goldsmith (since 2011)

Kwame Asante

Stone setter (since 2014)

Ravi Menon

Drawings and commissions (since 2016)

Ines Marlow

Founder, goldsmith

Ines founded the workshop on Wexley Street in 2011 to create jewellery built for daily life. She works at the bench peg shaping ring shanks and forging plain bands in recycled gold.

Kwame Asante

Stone setter
Since 2014

Kwame joined the bench in 2014, specializing in secure claw and flush stone settings examined under a loupe. He sets all commission stones and handles claw re-tipping for repairs.

Ravi Menon

Drawings and commissions

Ravi has guided commissions at the workshop since 2016, leading forty-five-minute bench talks with clients. He translates personal stories and heirloom remakes into precise scale pencil drawings.

Lea Brandt

Engraver
Since 2017

Lea has provided the bench's hand engraving since 2017. She carves custom lettering inside ring shanks and cuts crisp geometric designs onto signet faces.

Sofia Duarte

Polishing and repairs
Since 2019

Sofia joined the team in 2019 to oversee sizing, restoration, and hand-finishing at the bench. She cleans, re-polishes, and adjusts existing jewellery so it can continue being worn.

Hana Okada

The shop and fittings
Since 2021

Hana has welcomed visitors to the Wexley Street front room since 2021. She conducts ring fittings, coordinates bench talk appointments, and manages ready-made shop collections.

Founding and Commission Design

Ines Marlow founded Tsuya Jewellers in 2011 as an independent goldsmith bench dedicated to enduring, low-key jewelry. Ines fabricates our heavy shanks, melts down customer gold, and oversees workshop operations with quiet precision. Working closely with her since 2016 is Ravi Menon, who handles drawings and commissions. Ravi translates initial bench talk conversations into clear pencil drawings and carved wax models, determining the exact proportions and structural balance before metal is poured.

Setting and Traditional Engraving

Kwame Asante joined the workshop in 2014 as our stone setter. Kwame secures every gem under a stereo loupe, pushing claws and bezels down with steady hand pressure so stones sit low, tight, and protected from daily knocks. Lea Brandt, an engraver with the bench since 2017, cuts freehand monograms, inscriptions, and surface patterns into gold and silver using handheld steel gravers. Her work gives every signet ring and commissioned band an enduring tactile depth.

Finishing, Restoration, and Client Fittings

Sofia Duarte joined in 2019 to lead polishing and repairs. Sofia restores vintage gold shanks, re-tips delicate claws, and gives every finished piece its soft brushed luster or satin polish. Hana Okada joined in 2021 to manage the shop and client fittings. Hana welcomes visitors to 22 Wexley Street, coordinates bench talk schedules, and measures hands with calibrated sizing rings so every ring fits smoothly across the knuckle.

pages.title: About
pages.content:
About

Since 2011, Tsuya Jewellers has operated a working bench and quiet shopfront at 22 Wexley Street in Port Ellery. We believe jewelry should be made for ordinary days, built to wear in rather than wear out.

The Wexley Street Workshop

Ines Marlow opened our bench in 2011 with a single peg, a handful of Swiss files, and a belief that jewelry should not be preserved in velvet boxes. At 22 Wexley Street in Port Ellery, our workshop and shopfront share the same room. When you step through the door, you hear the scrape of files against gold, the hiss of the pickle pot, and the tap of the chasing hammer. There are no sales counters or polished window displays. We make rings, chains, and studs that belong in daily life, developing character through years of contact with door handles, bicycle grips, and garden soil.

Recycled Metals and Small Runs

We work exclusively in solid recycled 18k gold, 9k gold, and recycled sterling silver. Mass production polishes away the human touch, so we deliberately restrict our production to small runs and individual commissions. Each piece is cast or forged in small batches, after which all surfaces are filed, beveled, and finished by hand. We do not use plated metals or hollow stampings. Solid recycled metal ensures that our jewelry can be sized, repaired, and re-engraved decades from now without structural compromise.

The Bench, the Drawing, and the Hand

Every finished object begins with an honest drawing. Ravi Menon sits down with clients or sketches new forms in pencil at the bench. A green carving wax is sculpted by hand to test proportions and weight before metal is cast. Ines, Kwame, Lea, and Sofia then file the shank, set the stones, and carve the engraving. The final element is the hand that wears it. Jewelry only finds its true form once it settles into your daily routine and gathers the soft patina of ordinary life.

Built to wear in, not wear out.

A single ring on a linen tray under one lamp.

The drawing

The hand

Where the piece finds its shape.

pages.title: Sizing
pages.content:
Sizing

A ring should fit comfortably across the knuckle and rest easy at the base of the finger. We provide guidance to help you find your exact measurement before ordering.

How to Measure Your Ring Size

To determine your correct ring size, measure your finger at the end of the day when your hands are at a normal, warm temperature. Cold fingers are thinner, while swollen hands will yield an uncomfortably loose fit. If you already own a ring that fits the intended finger well, measure its inside diameter in millimeters using a rigid metal ruler or digital calipers. Measure across the widest internal opening, taking care not to include the metal rim itself. If your knuckle is significantly wider than the base of your finger, choose a size that sits halfway between the two measurements so the ring slides over the joint with slight resistance.

Ring Size Conversion Guide

Our conversion chart correlates United States sizes with European standards and internal millimeter diameters across our benchmark sizes. Because international measuring scales differ between jewelers, we calibrate our bench mandrels to record both diameter and circumference with complete consistency. When selecting a band from our collection, you can reference your established measurement in whichever regional system you prefer, or consult the conversion rows displayed here. For those visiting Port Ellery, Hana Okada can measure your finger directly at the bench counter using our calibrated metal sizing rings, ensuring the shank slides smoothly over the knuckle and rests comfortably in daily wear.

What if my new ring does not fit perfectly?

We provide free sizing within 30 days of purchase on all standard rings. If your ring feels too tight when your hands warm up, or if it spins loosely during cold weather, bring it into 22 Wexley Street or mail it back to our workshop. Sofia Duarte will adjust the shank up or down by hand. Standard gold resizing takes 7 days to complete, and we return the piece with a clean satin finish, fitting your hand as it was intended.

Book a fitting →

pages.title: Visit
pages.content:
Visit & Contact

Our shop and workshop share a single quiet room at 22 Wexley Street in Port Ellery. You are welcome to view ready pieces or sit down to talk through a commission.

Workshop Hours and Location

You can find us at 22 Wexley Street, Port Ellery. We are open Tuesday through Saturday from 11:00 to 19:00, with late hours on Thursday until 20:00. The workshop is closed on Sunday and Monday for uninterrupted bench fabrication days. Ready jewelry pieces are displayed in linen trays on our narrow wooden counter, and you are welcome to drop in during open hours to try on rings or inspect our chains.

Bench Talks and Consultations

If you wish to discuss a bespoke commission, reshape family jewelry, or select a stone, we recommend booking a bench talk. These appointments last 45 minutes and are entirely free. You will sit at the table with Ravi Menon or Ines Marlow to examine metal samples, review initial ideas, and take precise finger measurements. To reserve an appointment, use our contact form with your name, email address, preferred day, and a short description of what you have in mind.

Directions and Visiting Information

Our workshop is situated along Wexley Street, a quiet cobblestone lane just two blocks inland from the Port Ellery harbour front. Look for our understated entryway with a dark timber frame and a single warm lamp glowing in the front window. Street parking is available along Wexley Street and nearby side streets. If you have any questions before visiting, send a message through our contact form and Hana Okada will reply promptly.

Book a bench talk

Shipping & Returns

Pieces ship from Port Ellery within five working days, insured. Free sizing within 30 days: send the piece back and we resize it at no cost. Commissions are made to your drawing and are not returnable once the work has started.

posts.title: Two Bands from One Bracelet: Remaking an Heirloom at the Bench
posts.excerpt: How an unworn family bracelet brought to 22 Wexley Street was melted and forged into two enduring wedding bands.
posts.content:
In the autumn of last year, a client arrived at 22 Wexley Street carrying a small velvet pouch. Inside was a heavy gold link bracelet, inherited from a grandmother and unworn for nearly three decades. The links were thick, solid, and cast in warm 18k yellow gold, but the style was far too formal for the client’s daily life. Rather than leaving the gold tucked away in a dark drawer, the couple wanted to transform the single bracelet into two matching wedding bands that could be worn every day, through morning dishwashing, bicycle commutes, and quiet evenings at home.

They booked a bench talk on a Wednesday afternoon. At Tsuya Jewellers, these initial consultations last 45 minutes and are free of charge. Ravi Menon sat with the couple at the wooden table in our Port Ellery shopfront. Together, they weighed the bracelet, tested the purity of the metal, and discussed how the weight of the original piece could be divided evenly into two comfortable rings. The goal was not to produce delicate display pieces, but sturdy bands with low, rounded profiles that would sit quietly against the finger without catching on clothing or tools.

Within 10 days, Ravi completed detailed pencil drawings and an exact quote for the commission. A plain band commission in recycled 18k gold starts from $980, and the couple approved the drawings, confirming the work with our standard 40 % deposit. Before melting the grandmother's gold, Ravi hand-carved two green wax models for a fitting at the shop. Trying on the wax allowed the couple to test the width and thickness against their knuckles, ensuring the balance felt right in the hand before any heat touched the metal.

Once the wax fitting was confirmed, Ines Marlow took the bracelet to the bench peg. Founded in 2011, our workshop has always prioritized traditional bench fabrication over quick industrial casting. Ines carefully cleaned the links, snipped them into manageable segments, and placed them into a clay crucible under the torch. As the gold melted into a glowing pool, she cast a single rectangular ingot. Using our hand-cranked rolling mill, Ines rolled the ingot into a thick wire, annealing the metal with a gentle flame between passes to keep the grain supple and strong.

The wire was measured and cut into two lengths, one for each ring. Ines bent each piece around a steel mandrel, brazed the joints with high-karat gold solder, and filed the outer curves by hand using fine Swiss files. Sofia Duarte then brought both bands to the polishing lathe, giving the yellow gold a soft, satin brushed finish rather than a reflective mirror shine. The subtle texture highlights the warmth of the original alloy while concealing the tiny scratches that naturally accumulate through daily wear.

Six weeks from the approved drawing, the couple returned to 22 Wexley Street to collect the finished rings. What had spent thirty years as a forgotten bracelet in a drawer was now two distinct bands, ready to start a second life on two working hands. Like every piece made at our bench, they were built to wear in, not wear out, carrying an old family memory forward into ordinary Tuesdays for decades to come.
